You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From dd066823db2ac4e22f721ec85190817b58059a54 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Date: Wed, 12 Sep 2018 14:06:10 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] bpf/verifier: disallow pointer subtraction

Subtraction of pointers was accidentally allowed for unpriv programs
by commit 82abbf8d2fc4. Revert that part of commit.

Fixes: 82abbf8d2fc4 ("bpf: do not allow root to mangle valid pointers")
Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Acked-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>

diff --git a/kernel/bpf/verifier.c b/kernel/bpf/verifier.c
index 92246117d2b0..bb07e74b34a2 100644
--- a/kernel/bpf/verifier.c
+++ b/kernel/bpf/verifier.c
@@ -3163,7 +3163,7 @@ static int adjust_reg_min_max_vals(struct bpf_verifier_env *env,
 				 * an arbitrary scalar. Disallow all math except
 				 * pointer subtraction
 				 */
-				if (opcode == BPF_SUB){
+				if (opcode == BPF_SUB && env->allow_ptr_leaks) {
 					mark_reg_unknown(env, regs, insn->dst_reg);
 					return 0;
 				}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File Modified: `kernel/bpf/verifier.c`**
   - The `if` statement that checks for `BPF_SUB` operations has been modified to only allow pointer subtraction if `env->allow_ptr_leaks` is true. The line originally allowing all pointer math has been removed. This restricts the use of pointer subtraction in the BPF verifier, specifically for unprivileged programs.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The change reverts part of a previous commit (82abbf8d2fc4), which inadvertently allowed pointer subtraction for unprivileged programs. By enforcing the check on `env->allow_ptr_leaks`, the fix ensures that pointer subtraction is disallowed under conditions where it shouldn't have been permitted, thereby enhancing the safety and integrity of BPF programs. The patch addresses concerns raised by the reported issue and implements feedback from the community, indicating a collaborative effort to improve the BPF verifier.
